steps.evidence: docs/Contribute.md:71-72 (create DB e.g. 'lychee' and put credentials in .env)

notes: Dev setup lives in docs/Contribute.md (README only links to it; README's Installation section is a Docker quick-try of the published image, which is what readmeCommands holds, not a from-source dev setup). composer.json post-install-cmd (lines 149-152) already copies .env.example to .env and runs key:generate --no-override, so env-copy/key:generate happen automatically during composer install. Database: docs say create a DB and set credentials (php-mysql 'usually used for your local database'), hence mysql; but .env.example:67 defaults to DB_CONNECTION=sqlite (database/database.sqlite, which migrate offers to create), so a SQLite setup works with no DB server. CI tests mariadb/postgresql/sqlite. .env.example ships APP_ENV=production / APP_DEBUG=false; a developer may want local/true. Frontend uses the Vite+ CLI `vp` (package.json dev script = `vp dev`, so `npm run dev` / `npx vp dev` also work); CI installs with `vp install --frozen-lockfile` against package-lock.json (npm). The docs never say how to serve the PHP side: `php artisan serve` (or Valet/Herd/nginx) is inferred; `vp dev` only serves assets (or proxies API with VITE_LOCAL_DEV=true + VITE_HTTP_PROXY_TARGET=http://localhost:8000). PHP ^8.4 (composer.json:40); Node floor 24 from CI matrix (24, 26), no engines field. .gitmodules lists public/Lychee-front but there is no gitlink, so no submodule step. Contribute.md also lists many PHP extensions (imagick, exif, gd, bcmath, intl, redis...).
